transcript:
Meeting Header:
- Date/Time: 2026-07-01 15:00 PST
- Duration: ~45 minutes
- Attendees: Maya Patel (Redwood AE), Diego Alvarez (Redwood SE), Lena Cho (Redwood CSM), Sarah Kim (CISO - Ravenwood), Paul Reynolds (Lead Cloud Engineer - Ravenwood), Tina Morris (Prod Ops)

Summary:
Quick weekly POC security sync; primary topics SSO/SAML integration, audit logs & retention, SOC 2 evidence requests, and short discussion about private deployment options and KMS/encryption. Team agreed next steps and dates.

Topics:
1) SSO (Okta/SAML) test flow and metadata
2) Audit log export, retention and export formats
3) Data residency & retention policies during POC
4) SOC 2 evidence and timeline
5) Private/VPC connectivity and key management (KMS/HSM)

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll do about 45 minutes, um quick roll call?
[00:07] Sarah: Sarah here, CISO Ravenwood.
[00:09] Paul: Paul Reynolds, cloud eng.
[00:10] Tina: Tina Morris, ops.
[00:12] Diego: Diego from Redwood, SE on the account.
[00:14] Lena: Lena from CSM, hi.
[00:16] Maya: cool, thanks. first item SSO 
 d last week Paul attached the Okta metadata and had a couple questions about attribute mappings. Diego did you have a chance to validate?
[00:27] Diego: yeah i ran through it, there's one small mismatch on the nameID format, Ravenwood's sending transient and our test expects persistent, but we can accept either. also note group claim mapping sometimes comes back as "groups" vs "memberOf" and the auto-provisioning mapping in our console is a bit... finicky in the UI, so i'll share the xml and a step by step.
[00:48] Paul: ok that makes sense, we can change the app in Okta. any cert rollover concerns? we rotate certs every 90 days, do you support automatic metadata refresh?
[00:58] Diego: we support metadata url ingestion for SAML so you can host the metadata in Okta and we'll refresh, but if you use manual upload we'll need a new file on rollover. we'll also surface error logs if the signature validation fails.
[01:12] Sarah: is there an auditable event for SSO logins in your audit logs? we need to tie SSO success/failures back to our SIEM.
[01:20] Diego: yes we log auth events 
 d successful logins, failed attempts, session creation, token issuance 
 d and those are available in the Audit Logs API. the format is JSON lines, and we have a sample export script.
[01:33] Tina: what's retention on those logs during the POC? we have a 1 year retention expectation but for pilot maybe 90 days is ok if we get exports.
[01:43] Maya: we can set retention policy per-customer; default is 90 days for hosted, but you can set longer with a config if required. Diego can show how to export logs to your S3.
[01:55] Diego: right 
 d for hosted POC we offer log forwarding to customer S3 buckets or to a syslog endpoint, and you can also pull via the Audit Logs API. retention in our console is configurable, but export ensures you have canonical copies. i'll demo an export next week.
[02:10] Paul: export formats? we prefer compressed newline-delimited JSON, gzipped.
[02:15] Diego: we default to NDJSON gz, yes. timestamps are ISO8601. include actor, event_type, request_id, resource, and metadata. sometimes the model names get munged in transcription 
 d e g "redood" in logs, but request ids are stable.
[02:32] Sarah: encryption at rest and in transit? we need KMS integration and ability to use our AWS KMS keys for private deployments.
[02:40] Diego: for Redwood Hosted we manage encryption at rest and we offer customer-managed keys (CMK) via AWS KMS for Dedicated and Private. for Private (VPC/on-prem) you can provide HSM integration as well.
[02:52] Paul: how about audit evidence for SOC 2 
 d logs, change control, access reviews 
 d do you have a packaged set?
[02:58] Maya: yes we'll send the SOC 2 Type II report and a security overview deck. that covers control descriptions. Diego will also share a list of artifacts you can use for your vendor assessment.
[03:10] Sarah: timeline? we need to sign off our vendor assessment by end of month.
[03:14] Maya: we'll aim to deliver the SOC 2 report by 7/3. if you need more tailored evidence, Diego can map controls to artifacts.
[03:21] Diego: i can do a control mapping spreadsheet 
 d e g map CC6.1 to our access logs, CC7.2 to change control tickets 
 d i'll annotate with locations and export scripts.
[03:32] Tina: question on data residency 
 d during the POC some data will be processed in us-west regions but we have EU data sets. can you guarantee region pinning?
[03:41] Diego: we can pin model execution to region and we have EU regions for production; for hosted POC region pinning is possible but we'd need to confirm capacity. for strict residency we recommend Dedicated or Private where compute sits in your region.
[03:55] Paul: and on private connection 
 d we need a VPC endpoint, private egress, and no public internet outbound from models to satisfy compliance. how does Redwood handle that?
[04:04] Diego: Redwood Private can be deployed inside your VPC or via a private peering connection, and we support VPC endpoints for ingestion. outbound access can be restricted; for dependencies we can provide allowlists. some customers put a NAT for patching window but otherwise block egress.
[04:20] Sarah: what about data retention for embeddings and KV cache 
 d we need to ensure no persistent storage of PII beyond TTL.
[04:28] Diego: by default we do optional prefix/KV caching to improve latency; for POC we can disable persistent KV caching or set TTLs to a short window. embeddings storage is configurable 
 d we can mark those ephemeral and schedule a purge. we'll provide the purge API.
[04:42] Paul: do you do token-level redaction or PII masking?
[04:46] Diego: we have tooling for redaction at ingestion and a policy layer to zero out fields. not automatic by default, but SE can show policy rules in the Console.
[04:55] Tina: any concerns with e-discovery or legal holds? we may need to retain certain requests longer for investigations.
[05:02] Maya: that's doable 
 d we can create retention exceptions and export those records to your archive. we'll capture the workflow in the next week's demo.
[05:10] Paul: audit log integrity 
 d do you provide log signing or tamper evidence?
[05:15] Diego: we maintain append-only logs with immutable object store for audit trail in Dedicated/Private and signed manifests for hosted exports; i'll include details in the doc.
[05:25] Sarah: a hard ask 
 d we need to verify the identity of all Redwood engineers who will have console access, and SSO should be enforced. can we get a list?
[05:33] Maya: yes, we'll provide a list of named engineers who have access and their roles; SSO enforced for non-customer facing access. we'll redact personal emails unless required.
[05:43] Diego: small note on evidence: our SOC 2 package includes role-based access docs, change control tickets, and an inventory of engineers.
[05:51] Paul: any blockers from your side for us to test SAML in our staging org?
[05:55] Diego: no blockers 
 d send the staging Okta metadata and i'll configure a test app. if you want we can do a 30 min hands-on next Tuesday.
[06:04] Lena: i'll schedule that with Paul and Diego.
[06:07] Maya: last item 
 d are we still okay with the 90 day retention for the POC logs? Sarah?
[06:11] Sarah: for pilot yes 90 days is fine but we need export set up and proof of purge.
[06:16] Maya: agreed. we'll send the exports and purge APIs.
[06:19] Tina: one more ops question 
 d monitoring and alerting for unusual model activity, e g high cost or unexpected prompts?
[06:28] Diego: Console has per-route thresholds and alerting, and Optimize gives cost anomaly detection. We'll enable sample alerts to Ravenwood Slack channel.
[06:36] Paul: Slack integration ok but must be outbound to internal webhook only.
[06:40] Diego: yes we support customer-hosted webhooks.
[06:43] Maya: recap / next steps: i'll send SOC2 and deck, Diego will push SAML guide and audit log demo plan, we'll schedule the SAML hands-on and the on-prem feasibility call.
[06:55] Sarah: thanks everyone, that's it from Ravenwood.
[06:58] Maya: thanks, look forward to follow ups.
